suggestions.title: Arrival
suggestions.description: Mysterious spacecraft touch down across the globe, and linguist Louise Banks (Amy Adams) is recruited to decipher their language before the world's militaries jump to conclusions that could trigger a war. Denis Villeneuve's haunting, deeply human sci-fi masterpiece is less about aliens and more about communication, time, and the choices we make — a quiet, cerebral stunner with one of the most moving final acts in modern cinema.

suggestions.title: Knives Out
suggestions.description: When renowned crime novelist Harlan Thrombey dies right after his 85th birthday party, detective Benoit Blanc (Daniel Craig, gleefully chewing the scenery) is hired to untangle a family of suspects who all have motive, means, and opportunity. Rian Johnson's razor-sharp Agatha Christie homage is a dazzling modern whodunit — funny, twisty, impeccably cast (Chris Evans, Ana de Armas, Jamie Lee Curtis), and endlessly rewatchable.

suggestions.title: Let the Right One In
suggestions.description: Twelve-year-old Oskar, a lonely boy bullied at school, befriends the strange new girl next door, Eli — who only ever appears at night and never seems to get cold. Tomas Alfredson's Swedish masterpiece quietly reinvents the vampire film as a tender, chilling story of first love and quiet violence. Frostbitten, poetic, and unforgettable — a completely different kind of horror movie.
